notes: Rewritten after the operator source-of-truth document was removed from the corpus (see docs/ARCHIVED.md); this is a new precedence topic, not a rebuild of one of the four original fixtures. Built from tby-groundwater-lt5-19-01 (usgs-nfm-a6.7-turbidity.pdf: 'natural turbidity in ground water generally is less than 5 turbidity units. Natural ground-water turbidity of up to 19 turbidity units has been reported for some environmental settings'), used for both turns; the same chunk's next sentence, verified in data/corpus/corpus.json, reads 'Contaminated ground-water systems, however, can have considerably higher turbidity', used as a turn-2 guard against manufacturing a numeric cutoff out of it. No turbidity probe datasheet exists anywhere in the corpus (checked against all 14 documents), so there is no probe-measurement-span distractor available for this parameter the way pH and DO have one — the trap is the groundwater background figures themselves, tempted to be read as a pass/fail band. This fixture also carries the turbidity-specific system-prompt rule (src/prompt/systemPrompt.ts): turbidity is 'a relative, uncalibrated index' that must be characterised only qualitatively and 'never judge[d] against a numeric range', and get_pod_thresholds (TOOL_BLOCK) does not cover turbidity at all — so unlike pH or dissolved oxygen, no pod-configured numeric turbidity threshold can ever exist. That sharpens rather than breaks the class premise: the assistant must say so instead of ever substituting the document's figures for a verdict. Direct-feed's slice holds only the four probe datasheets, none of them turbidity, so it has no turbidity background material to draw on at all. Expected_to_favor is rag.

turns.content: Our groundwater well pod is showing turbidity of 12 NTU. Is that too high for our pod?

must_contain: States that the USGS turbidity chapter describes natural groundwater turbidity as generally less than 5 turbidity units, with values up to 19 units reported for some environmental settings, attributed to that chapter
Makes clear this is a description of what has been observed in groundwater, not a criterion or pass/fail band the chapter sets
States that turbidity is treated as a relative, uncalibrated index here and is not judged against a numeric range
States that no threshold is configured for this pod's turbidity
Declines to say whether 12 NTU is too high, normal, or out of range for the pod
must_not: declares 12 NTU normal, abnormal, too high, or in or out of range for the pod
presents the 'less than 5, up to 19' groundwater description as this pod's configured threshold
judges the reading against any numeric turbidity range or presents it as a calibrated measurement
invents a turbidity threshold that appears in no source

turns.content: So can we just flag anything over 19 NTU as a problem at our well pods?

must_contain: States that the chapter reports natural groundwater turbidity of up to 19 turbidity units in some settings, and that contaminated groundwater can run considerably higher, attributed to that chapter
States that the chapter's groundwater figures describe what has been observed, not a value it recommends flagging on
Reiterates that turbidity is a relative, qualitative indicator here, not a value with a numeric pass/fail band
States that no threshold is configured for this pod's turbidity
Declines to adopt 19 NTU, or any other figure, as the pod's flagging threshold
must_not: agrees to flag readings over 19 NTU as a threshold for the pod
states that the USGS chapter recommends or sets 19 as a criterion
invents an alternative numeric turbidity threshold
treats the chapter's statement that contaminated systems can have considerably higher turbidity as establishing a specific numeric cutoff
